title: Principal object still Christ grace and mercy (Stapleton; Trent sess.6)
source_text: XXII. Non negant tamen fidei justificantis objectum praecipuum & potissimum esse Dei gratiam & misericordiam in Christo peccatoribus credentibus atque poenitentibus per Evangelii promissiones oblatam. Id inter alios concedit & agnoscit Thomas Stapletonus, suamque hac in parte doctrinam verbis Concilii Tridentini confirmat, libro 8. de Justificatione, cap. 12. ubi loquens de facta per Christum redemptione, Hoc, inquit, objectum non unicum respicit fides, sed certe maxime & potissimum, quando hominem disponit ad justificationem. Quod & his verbis Patres Tridentini docuerunt, Sess. 6. cap. 6. Disponuntur ad justitiam credentes vera esse quae divinitus revelata & promissa sunt: atque illud in primis a Deo justificari impium per gratiam ejus, per redemptionem quae est in Christo. Fides ergo justificans, seu disponens ad justitiam, principaliter quidem respicit Christum ut Mediatorem, & redemptionem per illum factam, non tamen unicum & proprium est illud fidei justificantis objectum, ut volunt haeretici, cum tot praeterea alia objecta fides respiciat, dum ad justificationem disponimur, ut dictum est.
pass_a_gloss: They do not deny, however, that the chief and principal object of justifying faith is God grace and mercy in Christ offered through the Gospel promises to believing and repentant sinners. Among others Stapleton grants and acknowledges this, and confirms his doctrine here by the words of the Council of Trent, De Justificatione book 8, chapter 12, speaking of the redemption wrought through Christ: this object, he says, is not the only one faith regards, but certainly the greatest and principal when it disposes a person to justification. The Tridentine Fathers taught the same (Sess. 6, c. 6): people are disposed to justice when they believe that what was divinely revealed and promised is true, and especially that God justifies the ungodly by his grace through the redemption that is in Christ. Justifying faith, or faith disposing to justice, therefore principally regards Christ as Mediator and the redemption done through him, yet that is not the sole and proper object of justifying faith as the heretics claim, since faith regards many other objects as well while we are being disposed to justification.
pass_b_english: Rome still grants that justifying faith chief object is God grace and mercy in Christ offered in the Gospel to believing penitents; Stapleton confirms this from Trent sess. 6 c. 6.

Christ the Mediator and his redemption are principal when faith disposes to justification, yet not the sole proper object; faith also regards the other revealed objects while that disposition is underway.

lemmas.gloss: yet not the sole and proper

choices.why: Principal without exclusivity vs Reformed restriction charge.
